summary: Suniti Kumar Chatterji (1890–1977) was an Indian linguist and Indologist. He studied at Scottish Church College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta, University of London, and University of Paris under Jules Bloch, and served at the University of Calcutta and the Government of India.
Supree Kanjanapisarn is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Assumption University under the supervision of Veerachart Nimanong.

Surama Dasgupta (1907–1998) worked in philosophy and Indology. She studied at the University of Calcutta and under Surendranath Dasgupta, earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge, and served as Reader in Philosophy at the University of Lucknow.
Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Tribhuvan University under doctoral supervisor Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta (1887–1952) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Sanskrit College, Calcutta, and Cambridge under J. M. E. McTaggart and James Ward. He held posts at Chittagong, Cambridge, Presidency University, Sanskrit College, and Calcutta.
Surya Das (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University at Buffalo from ~1968 to 1971 and under traditional teacher Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

Suryya Kumar Bhuyan (1892–1964) was an Indian historian and Indologist. He earned degrees from Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and SOAS, and held posts including Principal of Cotton University and Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University.
Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü.
Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2004, where she studied under teachers including Stephanie W. Jamison and George L. Hart.
Susan L. Beningson is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr.
Susan L. Huntington (born 1943) is a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She was a professor at Ohio State University from approximately 1970 to 2011.
Susan Meinheit is a Tibetology scholar attested in posts at the Library of Congress in 1998 and 2007.

Susan Naquin (born 1944) is a historian and Sinologist. Educated at Stanford and Yale, she served as assistant professor of history at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

Susan Neiman (born 1955) is a philosopher who studied at Harvard and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and has served as Director of the Einstein Forum since 2000.
Susan Niditch (born 1950) is a religious studies scholar who served in the religion department at Amherst College from approximately 1978 to 2020.

Susan Whitfield (born 1960) is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. She earned her PhD from SOAS, directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017), and became Professor at UEA in ~2017.

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was a political scientist and Indologist who studied at Sarah Lawrence, Radcliffe, and Harvard. She taught political science at Harvard (~1955–1963) and served as a professor at the University of Chicago beginning in 1964.

Susanne Mrozik is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned degrees from Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University under Charles Hallisey, and held posts at Western Michigan University and Mount Holyoke College.

Sushanta Sen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at Visva-Bharati University, where he became a lecturer in 1986, and later served as Lecturer in Indian Religions at the University of Birmingham.

Sushil Kumar De (1890–1968) was an Indologist who studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, SOAS, and University of Bonn. He held professorships at the University of Calcutta and University of Dhaka, and headed the Bengali department at Jadavpur University.
